topic: Matrix Exponentials: The Engine of Continuous Change
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) with basic knowledge of Linear Algebra and Calculus.

sections.title: The Hook: The Growth of a Digital Colony
lecture_lines: Meet our digital colony: Cyber-Rabbits and Digital-Foxes.
A single population grows proportionally to its size.
But these two populations are coupled together.
Matrix A describes how their populations interact.
This linear system models their continuous evolution.
animations: Display a 'Cyber-Rabbit' icon (#00FF00) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] and a 'Digital-Fox' icon (#FF8C00).
Show the scalar growth equation $dx/dt = ax$ for one population.
Group populations into a vector $\mathbf{x}$ on the screen.
Introduce a 2x2 Matrix $A$ (#FFFFFF) representing their interactions.
Show the system equation $d\mathbf{x}/dt = A\mathbf{x}$ in large font.

sections.title: Prerequisite Bridge: The Taylor Series
lecture_lines: Recall the scalar exponential function's Taylor Series expansion.
Each polynomial term adds a layer of precision.
This infinite sum defines the curve's perfect shape.
animations: Plot the exponential curve $e^x$ on a coordinate graph.
Write the Taylor Series expansion $e^x = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2!} + \dots$ (#FFFFFF).
Successively add polynomial terms to the graph to fit the curve.

sections.title: The Leap: Defining $e^A$
lecture_lines: We can extend this series to square matrices.
Replace every scalar variable x with matrix A.
The number one becomes the identity matrix I.
Higher powers of A follow standard matrix multiplication.
The resulting sum defines the matrix exponential.
animations: Show the scalar Taylor series from the previous section.
Morph every scalar 'x' into a square matrix 'A' (#FFFFFF).
Transform the constant '1' into the Identity Matrix 'I' (#00FFFF).
Display the terms $A^2/2!$ and $A^3/3!$ as matrix powers.
Show the final sum $e^A = I + A + \frac{A^2}{2!} + \dots$ (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Computational Shortcut: Diagonalization
lecture_lines: Infinite sums are hard to calculate directly.
For diagonalizable matrices, we use the Eigen-shortcut.
Simply exponentiate the diagonal entries of D.
animations: Show a matrix $A$ decomposing into the product $PDP^{-1}$.
Display $e^D$ by exponentiating only the diagonal elements of $D$ (#FFFF00).
Show the final reconstruction $e^A = P e^D P^{-1}$ in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The Continuous Flow
lecture_lines: Matrix exponentiation represents a continuous transformation.
It maps an initial state to a future point.
As time flows, the coordinate grid warps smoothly.
The state follows a continuous trajectory through space.
This flow is the heart of linear dynamics.
animations: Setup a 2D coordinate grid with a starting vector $\mathbf{x}_0$ (#00FF00).
Display the time-dependent formula $\mathbf{x}(t) = e^{At} \mathbf{x}_0$.
Animate the grid warping smoothly as parameter $t$ increases.
Trace the vector's trajectory as a smooth, continuous path.
Highlight the movement as a 'flow' rather than a 'jump'.

sections.title: Application: Solving Systems of Differential Equations
lecture_lines: This provides the general solution for linear systems.
The matrix exponential acts as the system's propagator.
Watch the population levels evolve over time.
animations: Restate the system of differential equations $d\mathbf{x}/dt = A\mathbf{x}$.
Reveal the solution $x(t) = e^{At}x(0)$ as the 'Master Key' (#FFFFFF).

Graph the oscillating population levels for Rabbits [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] and Foxes [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg] over time.
